body:
HANDLES AND TRAPS (scanner.py and test_scanner.py read 6 Nov 2026, main 068c71a; B-40 has the proof).

THE LINES. `link_library` (scanner.py:74-117) treats an answer as complete when a page is shorter than `PAGE`, and an EMPTY first page is shorter: `complete = True`, then `_prune` (120-140) deletes every file row not seen. Only "no answer" (`songs is None`) is incomplete. The `Library` protocol the linker takes (scanner.py:30) has only `songs()`; the music server client already has `scan_status()` -> `{scanning, lastScan, count}` and `scanning()` (navidrome.py:131-139, used by the keeper at keeper.py:264). The linker never asks.

THE TEST THAT LIMITS THE RULE: test_a_file_that_is_gone_loses_its_row_and_nothing_a_person_has_changes (tests/test_scanner.py:98-115) removes ONE of TWO files and expects it pruned. B-40's "a floor of half" would refuse that exactly (1 of 2 is half). Choose the guard so a small library still loses one file: apply the floor only above a minimum size (for example 20 linked files), and always require the same absence on TWO passes for an empty answer. With a pass an hour apart a Host who really emptied the folder waits one hour; say that in the Host's page. Keep test_an_unanswered_music_server_prunes_nothing (118).

ASK THE MUSIC SERVER WHETHER IT IS SCANNING: no prune while `scan_status()` says `scanning`, and not on a pass whose answer is shorter than the previous pass by more than the floor. A restart in the middle of a scan is the second case of B-40 and the status call is the cheap proof. Add `scan_status` to the `Library` protocol and to `FakeLibrary` in tests/test_scanner.py.

TELL THE HOST: log and show "the music folder looks empty: is the disk mounted?" (a notification of the bell, kind `release` is not right; add a kind, docs/18 `notification.kind`). Do not tell members.

ORDER WITH P3-35 (B-60): both change `LibraryLinker`. Do P3-33 first: P3-35 makes passes happen the moment the music server finishes a scan, and a pass during a scan is exactly when answers are partial.

REPEAT: `python -X utf8 docs/evidence/scripts/audit_probes.py prune` (in-process; the wanted line says no files were pruned) and `audit_stack.py check prune` on a real stack. The B-40 end-to-end also showed the file feed growing from 7 to 17 rows: a pruned-then-relinked library re-announces every file to every phone; a refused prune avoids that churn.
